fda518a6 orca: say what dieWithParent = false costs `serve`; small test hardening
Review round 5, Important, DEFERRED (recorded here and in orca.nix):
with dieWithParent off, a signal to a running `orca-ide serve` CLI
(kill, an agent's timeout) kills the GUI's outer bwrap, which forwards
nothing, and leaves the Electron server running with the profile and
port. Ctrl-C (the whole foreground group) and a systemd cgroup stop are
unaffected. Not fixed here because the fix is to stop sandboxing the
GUI at all, which removes this and the `open` problem dieWithParent
works around; that is the separate orca-gui-unsandbox change, handed
this as a requirement. `serve` is not used on these hosts.

Tests: the GUI must not ship bin/orca either; the node-mode probe
exits on its own after 10s, since timeout reaches only bwrap; an empty
/etc/hostname falls back to uname -n, in both orca tests.

cf8d30ee orca: an explicit platform is upstream's rule again; drop a made-up reason
Review round 4. Round 3 narrowed the GUI wrapper's "caller named a
platform" test to `--ozone-platform=<value>`, on the claim that Orca's
display gate turns an empty value into X11. It does not: the gate treats
an empty value as unset and accepts either display, and Chromium keeps
the last of a repeated switch, so prepending before a bare or empty
`--ozone-platform` changed nothing. Back to Orca's own
hasExplicitOzonePlatform rule (bare or `=...`, before `--`), with the
bare and empty forms pinned in the argv cases.

The test's no-display probes also unset WAYLAND_SOCKET, which Orca
takes as a live Wayland display. Wording: the CLI's serve appends x11;
two orca-ide bins in the profile collide, not shadow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: 571ea2c0fac8

c8b36177 orca: test probes run with no display; an explicit platform has a value
Review round 3. Were node mode ever lost, the node-mode probe and the
lifetime case would each start a real GUI that `timeout` cannot reach
past bwrap; both now run without WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DISPLAY, so such a
launch exits at Orca's display gate instead of opening a window.

Only `--ozone-platform=<value>` counts as a caller's platform now: that
is what Orca's display gate reads, and a bare `--ozone-platform x11`
gives Chromium an empty value, which the gate turns into X11.

The PATH comment was backwards: env.nix puts the profile first by
design (an Orca-sandboxed shell is the exception), so were the screen
reader installed, `orca` would still be this CLI.

Tests: the argv harness ignores the caller's ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE,
refuses a wrapper with a second exec of the launcher, and falls back
when there is no nixGL layer; the lifetime case's parent stays up 4s,
for margin on a cold start, and still goes red with dieWithParent on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Entire-Checkpoint: cf0c875ebfc3

b1d69074 orca: an explicit platform is Orca's rule, not a prefix; test the GUI argv
Review round 2. The GUI wrapper took any argument starting with
--ozone-platform for a caller's own choice, so --ozone-platform-hint (a
preference, which Orca's gate ignores) dropped the wayland flag and left
Orca to pick X11 on a host with none. It now reads argv as Orca's own
check does: --ozone-platform or --ozone-platform=..., before any `--`.

Tests: the wrapper's argv decision, on the real generated script with
its exec swapped for printf, so nothing launches -- the prepend, the
caller's platform winning, the -hint and `--` cases, node mode. The
node-mode probe writes to a file instead of a pipe, and the lifetime
case runs only when node mode works: otherwise both would start a real
GUI that `timeout` cannot reach past bwrap.

Comments: why the wrapper is hand-written, /usr/bin before the profile
on PATH (bare `orca` is safe because the screen reader is absent, not
because of PATH order), the stale ~/.local/bin symlink.

63f565eb orca: CLI on plain node as `orca-ide`/`orca`, six agent skills; GUI is `orca-ide-app`
Install Orca's CLI the way upstream's .deb lays it out: `orca-ide` on
PATH is the CLI, and the GUI is off that name (here `orca-ide-app`, used
by the desktop Exec). Orca's skills tell agents outside an Orca terminal
to run exactly `orca-ide`; master had the GUI there, with an always-on
--ozone-platform=wayland that broke the GUI binary's own CLI dispatch
("Unknown flag --ozone-platform for command: open").

The CLI is plain JavaScript, so it runs on nixpkgs' nodejs_24 (Electron
43 bundles node 24) as a plain exec -- no sandbox between the caller and
the CLI. ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE points `orca-ide open` at the nixGL-wrapped
GUI; NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as upstream's shim does.

GUI: the wayland flag only outside node mode (`serve` probes the GUI
with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1, and Node rejects it); dieWithParent off,
since the GUI that `open` spawns is the CLI's direct child.

Six skills (orca-cli, orchestration, computer-use, orca-per-workspace-env,
orca-linear, linear-tickets) from stablyai/orca at the AppImage's own
sourceCommit; tests/orca-cli-skills.sh holds them to the hashes in the
build's current-manifest.json and the rev to the sourceCommit.

Supersedes the orca-cli-skills branch, which ran the CLI inside bwrap
and needed a hand-written signal forwarder to stop `serve` cleanly.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+host=$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null); HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.${host:-$(uname -n)}.config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }

+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` or `orca` -- in the profile they would collide.

+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done

+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide and orca to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi

+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.

+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"

+         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform=|--ozone-platform=" \
+         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
+         "-- --ozone-platform=x11|--ozone-platform=wayland -- --ozone-platform=x11"; do

+  got=$(argv $in)
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then pass "GUI argv: '$in' -> '$want'"
+  else fail "GUI argv '$in'" "got '$got', want '$want'"; fi

+else fail "GUI argv node mode" "got '$got'"; fi

+# ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
+# ("bad option", exit 9). With no display, and stdout to a file, not a pipe:
+# were node mode lost, this would be a GUI launch, which timeout cannot
+# reach past bwrap; without a display it exits before any window opens.
+nodisplay() { env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_SOCKET -u DISPLAY "$@"; }
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 10000).unref(); console.log("node-ok")' >"$T/node-out" 2>"$T/node-err"

+if [ "$(cat "$T/node-out")" = node-ok ]; then
+  node_ok=1; pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
+# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
+# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
+# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
+# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
+if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
+  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
+else
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"

+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
+else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
+fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: it works in a bash built without programmable
+# completion too.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() {
+  local u=() v
+  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
+  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
+}
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
+outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }

+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)

+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")
+  [ -n "$want" ] || { fail "$s" "no entry in the manifest"; continue; }

+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+

+[ "$fails" -eq 0 ]

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Cases for the claims orca.nix makes about the Orca CLI and its agent skills:
+# that `orca-ide` and `orca` are the CLI and run from any shell, not only an
+# Orca terminal; that the GUI is `orca-ide-app` and the CLI can launch it; and
+# that the skills in ~/.claude/skills are the bytes this Orca build expects.
+#
+# Why this needs a test. Orca's own installer only reaches an Orca terminal: it
+# puts a shim dir on PATH there (ORCA_CLI_BIN_DIR) and symlinks
+# ~/.local/bin/orca-ide at a raw /nix/store path, a script that runs Electron
+# against the host's libraries. The skills are stubs that tell the agent to
+# run `orca-ide skills get <name>` outside an Orca terminal, so a skill without
+# a working CLI under that name is a dead end. And the skills are pinned to a
+# commit separately from the AppImage version; bumping one without the other
+# silently installs guides for a different CLI. Orca ships the expected hashes
+# in resources/skills/current-manifest.json, so that is what the files are
+# held to.
+#
+# Usage:
+#   tests/orca-cli-skills.sh    eval + build this host's config and test it
+
+set -u
+set -o pipefail
+
+fails=0; n=0
+pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
+fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
+T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
+
+FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+# /etc/hostname is what CI writes to say which host it is; Orca's sandbox does
+# not bind it in, so fall back to uname -n there.
+host=$(cat /etc/hostname 2>/dev/null); HM="$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.${host:-$(uname -n)}.config"
+SKILLS="orca-cli orchestration computer-use orca-per-workspace-env orca-linear linear-tickets"
+
+pkg_attr() { # pkg_attr <pname> <attr>
+  nix eval --raw "$HM.home.packages" \
+    --apply "ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: (p.pname or \"\") == \"$1\") ps)).$2"
+}
+drv=$(pkg_attr orca-cli drvPath) || { echo "no orca-cli in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+want_version=$(pkg_attr orca-cli version) && [ -n "$want_version" ] \
+  || { echo "orca-cli has no version" >&2; exit 1; }
+CLI=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
+gui_drv=$(pkg_attr orca drvPath) || { echo "no orca in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
+GUI=$(nix-store --realise "$gui_drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
+echo "testing $CLI and $GUI"
+
+# The skills' own rule: outside an Orca terminal, on Linux, the CLI is
+# `orca-ide`; elsewhere it is `orca`. Both names must be the CLI, and the GUI
+# must not also claim `orca-ide` or `orca` -- in the profile they would collide.
+for b in orca orca-ide; do
+  if [ -x "$CLI/bin/$b" ]; then pass "orca-cli provides bin/$b"
+  else fail "bin/$b" "missing from $CLI"; fi
+done
+if [ -x "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca-ide" ] && [ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca" ]; then
+  pass "the GUI is orca-ide-app and leaves orca-ide and orca to the CLI"
+else fail "GUI bin names" "$(ls "$GUI/bin" | paste -sd' ')"; fi
+
+# No sandbox between the caller and the CLI: a plain exec of node, so
+# signals and exit codes are the CLI's own.
+if grep -q 'exec .*/bin/node ' "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" && ! grep -q bwrap "$CLI/bin/orca-ide"; then
+  pass "the CLI is a plain exec of node"
+else fail "CLI launcher" "$CLI/bin/orca-ide is not a plain node exec"; fi
+

+# ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE (without it, it fails, and `serve` refuses to start).

+# minus nixGL.

+  pass "orca open launches the profile's nixGL-wrapped GUI"
+else fail "ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE" "'${app:-unset}', want $GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"; fi
+

+# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=
+# wayland first, except in node mode or when the caller names a platform
+# itself -- `--ozone-platform` or `--ozone-platform=...` before any `--`,
+# the rule of Orca's own hasExplicitOzonePlatform; a -hint does not count.

+  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }
+argv() { env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE bash "$T/argv" "$@" | paste -sd' '; }

+         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform x11" \
+         "--ozone-platform=|--ozone-platform=" \
+         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
+         "-- --ozone-platform=x11|--ozone-platform=wayland -- --ozone-platform=x11"; do
+  in=${c%%|*}; want=${c#*|}
+  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+  got=$(argv $in)
+  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then pass "GUI argv: '$in' -> '$want'"
+  else fail "GUI argv '$in'" "got '$got', want '$want'"; fi
+done
+got=$(ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 bash "$T/argv" -e 1 | paste -sd' ')
+if [ "$got" = "-e 1" ]; then pass "GUI argv: node mode gets no flag"
+else fail "GUI argv node mode" "got '$got'"; fi
+
+# And for real: the CLI's `serve` probes ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE with
+# ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 and a script as argv, and Node rejects the flag
+# ("bad option", exit 9). With no display, and stdout to a file, not a pipe:
+# were node mode lost, this would be a GUI launch, which timeout cannot
+# reach past bwrap; without a display it exits before any window opens.
+nodisplay() { env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_SOCKET -u DISPLAY "$@"; }
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay timeout 60 "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" -e 'setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), 10000).unref(); console.log("node-ok")' >"$T/node-out" 2>"$T/node-err"
+node_ok=
+if [ "$(cat "$T/node-out")" = node-ok ]; then
+  node_ok=1; pass "orca-ide-app runs in node mode (serve's runtime probe)"
+else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi
+
+# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
+# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
+# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
+# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
+# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
+if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
+  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
+else
+ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
+  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
+  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
+for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
+if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
+else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
+fi
+
+# The manifest travels with the extracted AppImage, which the CLI's script
+# references, so it is in the CLI's closure.
+contents=$(nix-store -qR "$CLI" | while read -r p; do
+  [ -f "$p/resources/skills/current-manifest.json" ] && echo "$p"; done | head -1)
+[ -n "$contents" ] || { echo "no extracted AppImage in the closure of $CLI" >&2; exit 1; }
+manifest="$contents/resources/skills/current-manifest.json"
+
+# Outside an Orca terminal: none of its env, none of its shim dir on PATH.
+# ${!ORCA_@}, not compgen: it works in a bash built without programmable
+# completion too.
+clean_path=$(printf '%s' "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | grep -v 'linux-orca-cli-shim' | paste -sd:)
+outside() {
+  local u=() v
+  for v in ${!ORCA_@}; do u+=(-u "$v"); done
+  env "${u[@]}" PATH="$clean_path" "$@"
+}
+
+got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/orca" --version 2>&1)
+if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -qwF "$want_version"; then pass "orca --version reports $want_version outside Orca"
+else fail "orca --version" "got '$got', want $want_version"; fi
+
+# What every skill stub runs, under both names the stubs choose between.
+for b in orca-ide orca; do
+  got=$(outside "$CLI/bin/$b" skills get orca-cli 2>&1)
+  if printf '%s' "$got" | grep -q '^# Orca CLI'; then pass "$b skills get orca-cli prints the guide outside Orca"
+  else fail "$b skills get" "$(printf '%s' "$got" | head -3)"; fi
+done
+
+# A CLI failure is the CLI's exit status, not swallowed by a wrapper.
+outside "$CLI/bin/orca-ide" no-such-command >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?
+if [ "$rc" -eq 1 ]; then pass "an unknown command exits 1"
+else fail "exit status" "unknown command exited $rc"; fi
+
+# The rev is pinned by hand next to the version; the app knows its own.
+rev=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply 'f: f.".claude/skills/orca-cli".source' 2>/dev/null | sed -nE 's|.*-orca-skills-([0-9a-f]{40})/.*|\1|p')
+if [ -n "$rev" ] && grep -aqF "sourceCommit:\`$rev\`" "$contents/resources/app.asar"; then
+  pass "skills rev ${rev:0:8} is this build's sourceCommit"
+else fail "skills rev" "'${rev:-unparsed}' is not the sourceCommit in app.asar"; fi
+
+for s in $SKILLS; do
+  src=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply "f: toString f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source" 2>/dev/null) \
+    || { fail "$s" "no home.file .claude/skills/$s"; continue; }
+  # The source is a subpath of a fetch; realise the fetch's derivation itself.
+  srcdrv=$(nix eval --raw "$HM.home.file" --apply \
+    "f: builtins.head (builtins.attrNames (builtins.getContext f.\".claude/skills/$s\".source))" 2>/dev/null)
+  nix-store --realise "$srcdrv" >/dev/null
+  # Every file the manifest lists for the skill, as "<sha256>  <path>" lines.
+  want=$(jq -r --arg n "$s" '.skills[] | select(.name == $n) | .files[] | "\(.exactSha256)  \(.path)"' "$manifest")

+  if out=$(cd "$src" 2>/dev/null && printf '%s\n' "$want" | sha256sum --quiet -c - 2>&1); then
+    pass "$s matches this build's manifest ($(printf '%s\n' "$want" | wc -l) files)"
+  else fail "$s" "${out:-$src is missing}"; fi
+done
+

Round 6 review of origin/master..HEAD (fda518a6 down to 63f565eb). I found nothing Critical and nothing Important. There are three nits.

**What I checked**
- **Built outputs.** I evaluated shiori's outputs: the GUI is /nix/store/0539…-orca-1.4.238 and the CLI is /nix/store/xcsg…-orca-cli-1.4.238.
  - The GUI's bin/ has only `orca-ide-app` and `.orca-ide-unwrapped`. No `orca` or `orca-ide`.
  - The CLI's bin/ has `orca-ide` and `orca -> orca-ide`.
  - Every wrapper layer execs the next: the nixGL wrapper, nixGLCombinedWrapper-Intel, the hand-written orca-ide-app, then `.orca-ide-unwrapped`, which ends in `exec "${cmd[@]}"` for bwrap. There is no `--unshare-pid`. So the dieWithParent comment in orca.nix (lines 35-43) and the lifetime case's reasoning both hold.
- **The test's `inner` grep (orca-cli-skills.sh:79).** On the real nixGL script it picks the inner `/nix/store/071…/bin/orca-ide-app`, not the nixGL wrapper path, because `[^ ]*` cannot cross the space after the first path.
- **The node-mode probe (orca-cli-skills.sh:106).** I ran it myself, in node mode with no display and under `timeout 15`. It printed `node-ok` with argv `['a','b']` passed through, exited 0 in 0.22s, and left nothing behind. `.unref()` is correct: when the probe works, the timer does not hold the event loop open, so it exits at once. When something does hold the loop, the timer bounds the run at 10s, which is the case `timeout` cannot reach past bwrap. The FHS init's `source /etc/profile` puts nothing on stdout, so the exact `= node-ok` comparison is safe.
- **Hostname fallback.**
  - orca-cli-skills.sh:32 is correct.
  - sandbox-fonts.sh:37 nests `$(...)` with inner double quotes inside a double-quoted string, which is valid bash.
  - In this shell /etc/hostname is missing and `uname -n` prints `shiori`, so the comment at orca-cli-skills.sh:30-31 is accurate.
- **The bin/orca check (orca-cli-skills.sh:54).** It goes red if the GUI ships `orca` or `orca-ide`, apart from nit 1 below.
- **Comments against code.**
  - The ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE claim holds: in out/cli/runtime/launch.js and orca-app-executable.js, under plain node without it, `open` throws `runtime_open_failed` and `serve` throws `runtime_serve_failed`.
  - The NODE_OPTIONS handover matches upstream's shim in main/index.js (around lines 1154 and 1213).
  - The claim that tests/sandbox-fonts.sh finds the launcher by `.orca-ide-unwrapped` matches sandbox-fonts.sh:45.
  - The usage line `readlink ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide-app` resolves to the nixGL package, whose closure contains the unwrapped launcher.
  - sandbox-fonts.sh's pattern `.*orca-[0-9.]+` does not match `orca-cli-1.4.238`.
- **Does each case fail on a regression?** Yes for all of them:
  - The argv cases, against a wrapper that prepends the flag unconditionally or that goes back to prefix matching.
  - Node mode, against the flag added under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (Node exits 9 with no `node-ok`).
  - The lifetime case, against dieWithParent being turned back on (bwrap's parent is the `bash -c`, which exits at 4s).
  - The plain-exec, ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE, exit-status, rev and manifest cases.
- **Process cleanup.** The lifetime child exits itself at 7s. The test moves on at about 6s, so the child lives roughly 1s after the trap deletes $T, and by then it has nothing left to write. If the GUI starts slowly, the late `writeFileSync` into the deleted $T throws and the process exits. Its output goes to /dev/null, so no command substitution waits on it.

**Critical:** none.

**Important:** none.

**Nits**
1. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:54. `[ ! -e "$GUI/bin/orca" ]` (and the same for `orca-ide`) is true for a dangling symlink, which would still collide in the profile's bin/. Adding `&& [ ! -L … ]` would close that. This is unlikely to happen in practice.
2. tests/orca-cli-skills.sh:101-106. Nothing in the file explains the 10s self-exit; only fda518a6's commit message does. And if that timer ever fires, the probe still passes because `node-ok` was already printed, so a 10s hang in node mode passes silently. A one-line comment would cover it.
3. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh:37. The fallback copies the logic from orca-cli-skills.sh:32 but not its explanation (Orca's sandbox has no /etc/hostname). It is a cosmetic gap and the code is correct.
